title: AI-guided subtilisin variants improve aqueous amide formation
summary: The study reports that wild-type subtilisin BPN′ directly catalyzed condensation of free carboxylic acids and amines in aqueous PBS (pH 8, 40 °C), forming a peptide-bond amide without stoichiometric coupling reagents. The authors combined AI-guided mutation ranking with a FRET assay, reducing 7,999 in-silico variants at three active-site positions to five experimental candidates. The top triple mutant N155G/N218D/M222Q had reported relative activity of 753 ± 14% of wild type and also coupled biotin to a peptide fragment in water, extending beyond peptide–peptide ligation.
ai_technology: AI-guided enzyme mutation prediction combining binding-free-energy analysis of active-site substitutions with an experimental FRET-based rapid product-detection platform
organization: Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory; collaborating Chinese research institutions

evidence.tested: The study reports that wild-type subtilisin BPN′ directly catalyzed condensation of free carboxylic acids and amines in aqueous PBS (pH 8, 40 °C), forming a peptide-bond amide without stoichiometric coupling reagents.
evidence.unknown: The reported chemistry is demonstrated for specific peptide fragments and a biotin–peptide coupling example under the stated aqueous conditions; the paper does not establish broad substrate generality or production-scale utility. The 753% figure is reported relative catalytic activity with wild type as the reference, not a yield increase or 753-fold improvement. The reaction requires follow-up for broader substrate scope and process optimization.
evidence.ai_role: The AI-guided pipeline evaluated combinations at residues N155, N218 and M222, narrowing 7,999 in-silico variants to five prioritized mutants for FRET-based experimental validation. This reduced the candidate set and enabled selection of the N155G/N218D/M222Q variant; the AI component was applied after the paper established the wild-type aqueous amidation reaction.
